contents.name: 10.1.A Easy exercise: coproducts
contents.support: Disjoint-union gluing and unique component maps; empty coproduct is the empty scheme. Binary coproduct recalled inline, not confused with product.

contents.name: 10.1.2 Warning: products of schemes are not products of sets
10.1.4 Philosophy behind the proof of Theorem 10.1.1
contents.support: Five-stage affine/open gluing route, checked for arbitrary test schemes.

contents.name: 10.1.5: representable-functor reformulation
contents.reason: This is a second proof of the same existence theorem. The selected route is the complete direct gluing proof 10.1.1; no theorem in this batch requires the additional open-subfunctor formalism.

contents.name: 10.1.C Exercise (Yoneda lemma)
contents.reason: General representable functors and full faithfulness are not needed by the direct universal-property proof, which constructs and compares actual scheme morphisms.

contents.name: 10.1.6 Representable functors are Zariski sheaves
contents.support: Absorbed as the published gluing-of-morphisms property of actual schemes; no new site is introduced.

contents.name: 10.1.D Exercise: the product functor is a Zariski sheaf
contents.support: Glue the two compatible morphisms separately and use uniqueness to retain equality of composites.

contents.name: 10.1: open subfunctor definition preceding 10.1.E
contents.reason: Open subfunctors of arbitrary functors are specific to the optional representability proof; actual open subschemes suffice for the chosen construction.

contents.name: 10.1.E Exercise: intersection of open subfunctors
contents.reason: Intersection in a category of arbitrary functors is not a dependency of the scheme gluing construction; the corresponding actual open intersection is proved in open restriction.

contents.name: 10.1.F Exercise: open restriction of a product
10.1: open-cover definition preceding 10.1.G
contents.support: Actual affine open covers are used in the existence proof; arbitrary-functor cover terminology is not needed.

contents.name: 10.1.H Key exercise: local representability implies representability
contents.reason: The general Zariski-sheaf representability criterion exceeds the direct scheme gluing theorem used here. Its fibre-product application is proved, with the same gluing argument, by the existence theorem.

contents.name: 10.2(2) Adding an extra variable
contents.support: Polynomial universal properties give coefficient extension.

contents.name: 10.2.2 Remark: Galois tensor decomposition
contents.reason: The finite Galois generalization and torsor interpretation extend the selected quadratic splitting example; no argument here uses the general Galois decomposition. The unqualified printed wording must not be extended to infinite Galois products.

contents.name: 10.2.E Exercise: absolute Galois group as a spectrum
contents.reason: The profinite-topology description for the algebraic closure of Q is an arithmetic extension, independent of the construction and scheme-fibre computations in this page.

contents.name: 10.2.H Exercise: intersection of locally closed subschemes
10.2.I Exercise, affine-space part
contents.support: Record A^n_C as coefficient extension of A^n_A; same polynomial identity works for arbitrary rings, including Z.

contents.name: 10.2.I Exercise, projective-space part
contents.reason: The construction of projective spaces over arbitrary bases and their projective morphisms belongs with the relative projective treatment; the present affine chart formula supplies its input.

contents.name: 10.2.J Exercise: transcendental complex points
contents.reason: Closed points of Spec(Q(t) tensor_Q C) give an infinite transcendence example beyond the selected finite-presentation fibre calculations. No result in this scaffold requires its classification.

contents.name: 10.2.K Exercise: first view of a blow-up
contents.reason: The incidence equation xv=yu, exceptional P^1 and Cartier property are the introductory blow-up calculation and should be authored with exceptional divisors.

contents.name: 10.2.4 The graph of a rational map
contents.reason: Scheme-theoretic closure of a rational graph, with integral source and separated target qualifications, is needed for blow-ups as graph closures; here only graphs of everywhere-defined morphisms are constructed.

contents.name: 10.2.L Exercise: independence of rational-graph representative
contents.reason: Representative independence belongs to the rational-graph closure construction, not the everywhere-defined graph universal property on this page.

contents.name: 10.2.M Exercise: blow-up as graph of a rational map
contents.reason: The map (x,y) to [x:y] and its exceptional fibre are reserved for the blow-up pair, which owns the incidence construction.

contents.name: 10.3 Pulling back families and fibers of morphisms
10.3.1: family y^2=x^3+tx under t=uv
contents.support: Retain the source example as an inline illustration of substitution of coefficients, including t=3. The separate xy=t example is explicitly generated.

contents.name: 10.3.A Exercise: topological fibres
contents.support: Recall the induced-subspace topology and the categorical topological fibre as motivation, proving the scheme assertion via prime correspondence.

contents.name: 10.3.B Exercise: underlying topology of the scheme fibre
10.3.D Exercise: Gaussian integer fibres
contents.reason: The arithmetic splitting classification by congruence class of primes is not a prerequisite of the base-change theorems. The quadratic family already treats split, ramified, inert and generic ring behaviours without a separate arithmetic classification.

contents.name: 10.3.E Exercise: self-product of a quadratic cover
10.4.A Easy exercise: locally principal pullback
contents.support: One generator remains one generator in the extended ideal; do not conclude that a non-zero-divisor remains one without flatness.

contents.name: 10.4.B(b) Exercise: quasi-separated
contents.reason: Stability of quasi-separated morphisms is proved with the diagonal criterion; this batch constructs the diagonal/base-change identity for that next page.

contents.name: 10.4.B(d) Exercise: finite
contents.reason: Finite morphisms and finite module charts are owned by the finite/proper/projective pair; none is needed for the explicitly computed fibre coordinate rings here.

contents.name: 10.4.B(h) Exercise: finite presentation
contents.reason: The global finite-presentation conclusion additionally needs quasi-separatedness and its base-change stability; it is routed with that criterion, while the locally finite-presentation assertion is fully proved here.

contents.name: 10.4.C Exercise: quasi-finite
contents.reason: Quasi-finite morphisms and their finiteness over a field require the finite-morphism development; mere finite point sets are explicitly not claimed stable here.

contents.name: 10.4.E Exercise: integral products over algebraically closed fields
10.4.F Exercise: product stability of a property
contents.support: Factor f times g as the base change of f followed by the base change of g. State the conditional result only when the property is also composition-stable.

contents.name: 10.4.2 Properties not preserved by base change
10.4.3: geometric adjectives
contents.support: Use the design-requested algebraic-closure convention; the source also describes the all-algebraically-closed-field convention. Their equivalence is not used as a premise here.

contents.name: 10.4.H Exercise: stability of geometric fibre properties
contents.reason: This exercise uses geometric fibres over all algebraically closed extensions. The design here specifies tests at a chosen algebraic closure only; extending that convention to universal field tests and proving stability is a separate descent theorem, not a premise of any included proof.

contents.name: 10.4.I Exercise: geometric fibres of Spec C over Spec R
10.4.J Exercise: geometric quadratic fibres
contents.support: Over algebraic closures in characteristic zero the nonzero quadratic fibres split into two reduced points, while the zero fibre remains a dual number scheme.

contents.name: 10.4: table (Ra)–(Rd), (Ia)–(Id), (Ca)–(Cd)
contents.reason: The full comparison with perfect/separable closures and arbitrary fields is beyond the chosen-closure definition. The table is read to distinguish these conventions, not treated as an established dependency.

contents.name: 10.4.K(a) Exercise: field scalar-extension injection
contents.support: Choose a vector-space basis containing 1; this gives the nonzero tensor product needed for surjectivity.

contents.name: 10.4.K(b–d) Exercise: implications between field tests
contents.reason: Implications for reducedness, irreducibility and connectedness across all extensions form the separate field-descent comparison, which is not asserted by the chosen-closure definitions or the direct ring examples.

contents.name: 10.4.4 Hard fact: equivalence of field tests
contents.reason: No later statement here uses the difficult perfect/separable-closure criterion or the arbitrary-extension equivalence. It is not silently cited to justify base-change stability of geometric adjectives.

contents.name: 10.4.5 Universally injective (radicial) morphisms
contents.reason: Universal injectivity and inseparable-residue-field characterizations are a separate morphism class, beyond the design inventory. The counterexample to ordinary injectivity and positive immersion facts are retained.

contents.name: 10.4.L first (a): immersions are universally injective
contents.support: After any base change these remain immersions and thus injections on points.

contents.name: 10.4.L remaining parts: radicial residue fields, stability, cancellation
contents.reason: These characterize and organize the radicial class, which no included fibre or base-change theorem invokes; the example explaining its motivation remains included.

contents.name: 11.1.10 proof: Cartesian square of diagonals
contents.support: Only the displayed diagonal square is imported, without using separatedness to prove it.

contents.name: 11.1.10 Proposition: separated/quasi-separated base-change stability
contents.reason: The next pair owns the separated and diagonal-quasi-separated criteria; the present page proves exactly the categorical square that those stability proofs use.

contents.name: 11.1.18 Proposition, proof diagram (11.1.18.1)
contents.support: The graph square is Cartesian independently of any separation hypotheses.

contents.name: 11.1.18 Proposition: immersion/closedness/quasi-compactness of graph
contents.reason: These conclusions require the separation properties of the target diagonal, which are owned by the next pair. Polynomial graph closedness is instead directly verified by its quotient ring here.

contents.support: Field-valued points supply the canonical residue-field morphism.

contents.name: Lemma 26.13.1
contents.support: Include local-ring-valued version: all points map into any open containing the image of the unique closed point.

contents.name: Equation 26.13.1.1
contents.support: Canonical Spec of stalk map precedes its residue-field specialization.

contents.name: Lemma 26.13.2
contents.support: The local-base variant has image the generalizations; use prime localization.

contents.name: Lemma 26.13.3
contents.support: Include equivalence classes and the minimal residue-field representative; common extension of two fields follows by a nonzero tensor product and maximal ideal, proved inline from vector-space bases.

contents.name: Lemma 26.19.4
contents.support: Composition follows by applying the quasi-compact inverse-image definition twice.

contents.name: Lemma 26.19.5
contents.support: Closed immersions are affine; affine inverse images are quasi-compact, using the just-proved local criterion.

contents.name: Example 26.19.6
contents.reason: The infinite-variable punctured spectrum illustrates non-quasi-compact open immersions; the batch does not claim open immersions are quasi-compact and this separate example is not required by the design.

contents.name: Lemma 26.19.7
contents.reason: Closed image versus specialization-stable image is a preliminary for proper/closed morphisms; no fibre-product existence or affine ring calculation here uses the image-closure criterion.

contents.name: Lemma 26.19.8
contents.reason: The specialization-lifting criterion for closed maps belongs with universally closed and proper morphisms, beyond the base-change properties selected here.

contents.name: Lemma 26.21.1
contents.reason: The closed affine diagonal via multiplication B tensor_A B to B is the opening separation result of the next pair. The polynomial graph example proves its special quotient directly.

contents.name: Lemma 26.21.2
contents.reason: The general diagonal immersion theorem belongs with separation axioms; the present graph pullback identity does not use it.

canonical.name: def-fibre-product-schemes-universal-property
canonical.support: The scheme fibre product represents compatible pairs of morphisms from every test scheme T; define its projections and Cartesian square. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.17.1. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-fibre-product-unique-canonical-isomorphism
canonical.support: Two fibre products of the same diagram have a unique projection-compatible isomorphism. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.1.3 and 10.1.5. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: thm-affine-fibre-product-tensor-ring
canonical.support: Spec B times over Spec A Spec C is canonically Spec(B tensor_A C), as a product in all schemes. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.1.B; Stacks 26.17.2. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-affine-fibre-product-projections-stalk-maps
canonical.support: At a prime r of B tensor_A C, projections contract r to q in B and q-prime in C; the local maps are B_q to (B tensor_A C)_r and C_q-prime to that stalk and induce compatible residue-field embeddings. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.17.2 and 26.17.5. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-fibre-product-open-restriction
canonical.support: If P=X times_S Y exists, open V in X and W in Y mapping to an open U in S have product p-inverse(V) intersect q-inverse(W), an open subscheme of P. Also X times_S U=f-inverse(U). Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.17.3; Vakil proof 10.1.1 Step 1. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-fibre-products-glue-over-open-covers
canonical.support: If Y is covered by open Y_i and products X times_S Y_i exist, their inverse images over overlaps glue to X times_S Y. The analogous assertion holds for a cover of S. Support and dependency route: Vakil proof 10.1.1 Steps 2–5. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: thm-fibre-products-of-schemes-exist
canonical.support: Every pair of scheme morphisms X to S and Y to S admits a fibre product, covered by Spec(B tensor_A C) for compatible affine charts. Support and dependency route: Vakil Theorem 10.1.1, complete proof; Stacks 26.17.4. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: cor-product-schemes-over-base-exists
canonical.support: The category of S-schemes has binary products, terminal object S, and empty scheme as initial object; a product with the empty scheme is empty. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.1.1 and 10.1.A (empty gluing specialization). Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-fibre-product-associativity-and-symmetry
canonical.support: There are natural symmetry, associativity and unit isomorphisms for products of S-schemes, compatible with every projection. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.1.3; proof 10.1.1 Step 1. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: def-base-change-morphism-schemes
canonical.support: For S-prime to S, define X_S-prime=X times_S S-prime and f_S-prime on both structure morphisms and morphisms of S-schemes. A property is stable under base change if every such pullback retains it. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.18.1 and 26.18.3. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-base-change-composition
canonical.support: Iterated base change along S-double-prime to S-prime to S is canonically base change along the composite, functorially in objects and morphisms. Support and dependency route: Vakil proof 10.1.1 Step 1; 10.3.C. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-tensor-ring-presentations-for-base-change
canonical.support: For A-algebra C, base extension of A[t_i]/I is C[t_i]/I C[t_i]; base extension of S-inverse A is image(S)-inverse C, with no flatness assumption. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.2.A, B, F. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-field-valued-points-of-schemes
canonical.support: Morphisms Spec K to X are pairs (x, embedding kappa(x) to K); in particular Spec kappa(x) to X is canonical and compatible with scheme morphisms. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.13, paragraphs preceding 26.13.3 and its field-valued special case. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: def-scheme-theoretic-fibre
canonical.support: For any point s of S define X_s=X times_S Spec kappa(s), as a kappa(s)-scheme; allow nonclosed points, generic fibres and empty fibres. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.18.4; Vakil 10.3.2. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: thm-affine-fibre-coordinate-ring
canonical.support: For A to B and p in Spec A, the fibre is Spec(B tensor_A kappa(p))=Spec((A minus p)-inverse B / p(A minus p)-inverse B). Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.3.2; Stacks 26.18.4–5. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-points-of-fibre-primes-over-point
canonical.support: The map X_s to X is a homeomorphism onto f-inverse(s), with kappa(x in X_s)=kappa(x in X); in an affine chart these are exactly primes q of B with q intersect A=p. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.18.5; Vakil 10.3.B. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-scheme-fibre-stalk-quotient
canonical.support: At x above s, O_(X_s),x is O_X,x / m_s O_X,x, equivalently O_X,x tensor over O_S,s kappa(s). Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.18.6. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-points-of-scheme-fibre-product-residue-tensors
canonical.support: Points of X times_S Y correspond to (x,y,s,r) with common image s and r a prime of kappa(x) tensor_kappa(s) kappa(y); the residue field is that of r. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.17.5. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-fibre-after-base-change
canonical.support: If s-prime maps to s, the fibre of X_S-prime over s-prime is canonically X_s times_kappa(s) Spec kappa(s-prime). Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.3.C. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-base-extension-field-coordinate-ring
canonical.support: For a k-scheme X and field extension K/k, affine charts of X_K have rings A tensor_k K, compatibly on overlaps. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.2.3. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: def-geometric-fibre
canonical.support: Choose an algebraic closure Omega of kappa(s); define X_bar-s=X_s times_kappa(s) Spec Omega. A geometric point more generally has algebraically closed residue target; this page uses algebraic closures for fibre tests. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.4.3 and table (Rc), (Ic), (Cc). Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-geometric-fibre-choice-independent
canonical.support: Two choices of algebraic closure give isomorphic geometric fibres after transport of scalars by a chosen base-field isomorphism; no canonical choice is asserted. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.4.3 and scalar extension 10.2.3. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: def-geometrically-reduced-integral-connected-fibre
canonical.support: Call a fibre geometrically reduced, integral, irreducible or connected when its base change to an algebraic closure has that property. Integral and irreducible require nonemptiness; the empty scheme is reduced and connected under the no-separation convention. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.4.3 and table preceding 10.4.K. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-base-change-open-closed-immersions
canonical.support: Open and closed immersions remain so under arbitrary base change; immersions (equivalently, locally closed immersions) do also. The pulled-back closed ideal is the image of the pulled-back ideal in the new structure sheaf. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.17.6 and 26.18.2. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: def-scheme-theoretic-inverse-image-subscheme
canonical.support: Define the scheme-theoretic inverse image of a closed or locally closed subscheme Z of S under X to S as X times_S Z. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.17.7. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-subscheme-intersection-fibre-product
canonical.support: The intersection of finitely many closed subschemes of X is their fibre product over X and is cut out by the sum of their ideals; locally closed intersections follow by restriction. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.2.C and H. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-base-change-locally-finite-type-presentation
canonical.support: Locally finite type and locally finite presentation morphisms remain so after arbitrary base change. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.4.B(e,g); Stacks 29.15.4 and 29.22.4. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-base-change-quasi-compact-morphisms
canonical.support: Quasi-compactness is local on an affine cover of the target and is preserved by arbitrary base change. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.19.2–3. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: cor-base-change-finite-type-and-products
canonical.support: Finite type morphisms remain finite type under base change; products of two locally finite type (respectively finite type) k-schemes have the same finiteness property. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.2.D and 10.4.B(f). Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: def-affine-morphism-schemes
canonical.support: A scheme morphism is affine if the inverse image of every affine open is affine. Support and dependency route: Stacks 29.11.1. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-affineness-from-unit-generating-global-sections
canonical.support: If finitely many global sections f_i generate the unit ideal and all nonvanishing opens X_f_i are affine, then X is affine. Support and dependency route: Stacks 28.28.3, with elementary finite-equalizer proof. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-affine-morphism-local-on-target
canonical.support: A morphism is affine if the target has an affine open cover with affine inverse images. Support and dependency route: Stacks 29.11.3(1) iff (2), Remark 29.11.4; 26.11.5–6. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-base-change-affine-morphisms
canonical.support: Affine morphisms remain affine after arbitrary base change; compositions of affine morphisms and closed immersions are affine. Support and dependency route: Stacks 29.11.8–10. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: def-diagonal-morphism-scheme
canonical.support: Define Delta_X/S:X to X times_S X as the unique morphism with both projections identity. Support and dependency route: Stacks 26.21 introductory definition. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-diagonal-base-change-identification
canonical.support: Under (X_S-prime times_S-prime X_S-prime) isomorphic to (X times_S X)_S-prime, the diagonal is the base change of Delta_X/S. Support and dependency route: Vakil proof 11.1.10, pp.230–231. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: def-graph-morphism-over-base
canonical.support: For an S-morphism f:X to Y, define Gamma_f=(id_X,f):X to X times_S Y. Support and dependency route: Vakil 11.1.17, p.232. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-graph-as-pullback-diagonal
canonical.support: The graph square with X to X times_S Y above Y to Y times_S Y is Cartesian, with right arrow (f composed with pr_X,pr_Y) and left arrow f. Support and dependency route: Vakil proof 11.1.18, diagram (11.1.18.1), p.232. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: thm-classical-product-agrees-scheme-product
canonical.support: For irreducible classical varieties over an algebraically closed k, the associated scheme of the classical product is the scheme product of the associated schemes; affine chart rings are the unreduced tensor products, which here are domains. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.1.3 and 10.4.E; local published affine product theorem. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-base-change-surjective-morphisms
canonical.support: Surjective morphisms of schemes remain surjective under arbitrary base change; in particular extension of the ground field does not turn a nonempty scheme into an empty scheme. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.4.D. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: lem-immersions-and-localizations-monomorphisms
canonical.support: Open immersions, closed immersions and Spec(S-inverse A) to Spec A are monomorphisms of schemes; hence so are their composites. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.2.G. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: rem-properties-can-change-after-field-extension
canonical.support: Ordinary reducedness, irreducibility, integrality and connectedness need not survive scalar extension: C tensor_R C splits, while F_p(u) tensor_F_p(u^p) F_p(u) contains nilpotents. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.4.1–2 and 10.4.G. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: rem-fibre-is-scheme-not-point-set
canonical.support: A fibre retains its residue fields and nilpotents even though its underlying topology is the inverse-image topology; the underlying set of a general fibre product need not be a set product. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.1.2 and 10.3.3; Stacks 26.18.5–6. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: ex-fibre-family-xy-equals-t
canonical.support: For k[x,y,t]/(xy-t) over k[t], the fibre at a in k is Spec k[x,y]/(xy-a): at zero two reduced axes, at nonzero a a copy of G_m; the generic fibre has ring k(t)[x,x-inverse]. Support and dependency route: Specialization of the polynomial fibre computation in Vakil 10.3.1–2. This is a generated specialization, not a heading or example claimed to occur in the source.

canonical.name: ex-nonreduced-fibre-x-squared-equals-t
canonical.support: The family k[x,t]/(x^2-t) has special fibre k[x]/(x^2) in every characteristic. Over Q the fibres at 1, 0, -1 and the generic point are respectively Q times Q, Q[epsilon]/epsilon^2, Q(i), Q(x) over Q(t). Support and dependency route: Vakil Example 10.3.3(i)–(iv). Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: ex-base-change-real-conic-to-complex
canonical.support: The real affine conic Spec R[x,y]/(x^2+y^2+1) has no R-valued points, but its complex base change has point (i,0) and ring C[x,y]/(x^2+y^2+1). Support and dependency route: Polynomial scalar-extension method, Vakil 10.2.A–B and 10.2.3. This is a generated specialization, not a heading or example claimed to occur in the source.

canonical.name: cex-domain-tensor-algebraic-closure-reducible
canonical.support: An integral R-scheme need not stay irreducible or connected over C: Spec C becomes Spec(C times C), also showing injectivity need not survive base change. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.2.1, 10.4.1–2 and 10.4.I. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: ex-product-affine-lines-plane
canonical.support: A^1_k times_k A^1_k is A^2_k functorially; points over the pair of generic points are not unique, for instance primes (0) and (y-x) have the same contractions. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.1.2–3. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: ex-fibre-closed-immersion
canonical.support: The fibre of Spec(A/I) to Spec A over p is Spec kappa(p) if I is contained in p, and empty otherwise. Support and dependency route: Direct special case of Vakil 10.2.B and 10.3.2. This is a generated specialization, not a heading or example claimed to occur in the source.

canonical.name: ex-graph-polynomial-map-closed-subscheme
canonical.support: For f:A^n_k to A^m_k given by polynomials f_j, its graph has ideal (y_j-f_j(x)) in k[x_1,...,x_n,y_1,...,y_m]. Support and dependency route: Affine specialization of Vakil 11.1.17–18. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: cex-set-theoretic-fibre-loses-multiplicity
canonical.support: The zero fibres of x^2=t and x^3=t have the same one-point underlying space and residue field k, but are nonisomorphic schemes, of k-vector-space dimensions 2 and 3. Support and dependency route: Variant of Vakil 10.3.3(ii). This is a generated specialization, not a heading or example claimed to occur in the source.

canonical.name: ex-empty-fibre-tensor-zero-ring
canonical.support: The open immersion Spec k[t,t-inverse] to Spec k[t] has empty fibre at t=0 because its fibre tensor ring is zero. Support and dependency route: Direct localization special case of Vakil 10.2.F and 10.3.2. This is a generated specialization, not a heading or example claimed to occur in the source.

canonical.name: cex-purely-inseparable-base-change-nonreduced
canonical.support: For k=F_p(v), L=k[u]/(u^p-v) is a field but L tensor_k L is L[epsilon]/(epsilon^p), so reducedness need not survive even algebraic scalar extension. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.4.G. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.

canonical.name: ex-quadratic-cover-self-fibre-product
canonical.support: For t maps to x^2, the self fibre product of A^1_k over A^1_k is Spec k[x,y]/(x^2-y^2): two distinct line components if char k is not 2, a doubled diagonal if char k=2. Support and dependency route: Vakil 10.3.E. Exact claim qualifications and proof route are in the manifest and item checkpoint.
